string-array.item: How do I add a service

string-array.name: faq_bodies
string-array.item: CometOTP is a simple and free two-factor authenticator. It generates time-based one-time passwords (TOTP), counter-based passwords (HOTP), Steam codes and mOTP codes for the services you protect with two-factor authentication.\n\nEverything is stored encrypted on your device and never leaves it unless you create a backup yourself.

A one-time password (OTP) is a short code that is only valid once and, for time-based codes, only for a short period of time (usually 30 seconds).\n\nWhen a service asks you for a code, open CometOTP, find the service and type in the code shown on its card before the countdown runs out.

Two-factor authentication (2FA) is turned on in each service's own security settings, not in CometOTP. Depending on the service it is called two-factor authentication, 2-step verification or login verification. The steps are much the same everywhere:

1. Sign in to the service, on its website or in its app, and open its security settings.
2. Choose to set up two-factor authentication with an authenticator app. The service shows a QR code and, usually, a setup key.
3. In CometOTP, tap the + button and choose Scan QR Code, or choose Setup Key and type the key in.
4. Type the code CometOTP shows into the service to finish.
5. Keep the backup or recovery codes the service gives you somewhere safe. They let you sign in if you lose your phone.

The help pages below show where to find it for some popular services.

Tap the + button on the home screen and choose one of the options:

• Scan QR Code: point the camera at the QR code shown by the service.
• QR Code from Image: pick a screenshot or photo of the QR code.
• Setup Key: type the secret key and the account details by hand.

Backups are created from the Backup & Restore screen in the main menu. If the backup fails, make sure you have granted access to the folder you picked and that there is enough free space.\n\nAutomatic backups additionally need a default backup location and a backup password, both of which are set in Settings.

Time-based codes depend on the clock of your phone. Make sure that automatic date & time is enabled in your device settings.\n\nIf the codes are still rejected, remove the service from the website and add it to CometOTP again.

Create an encrypted backup on your old phone from the Backup & Restore screen, copy the file to your new phone and restore it there.\n\nCometOTP does not sync your accounts to the cloud, so a backup is the only way to move them.

Your accounts are stored in an encrypted file. The key is either kept in the Android KeyStore (hardware backed on most devices) or derived from your password or PIN, depending on the encryption method you chose during setup.\n\nYou can additionally lock the app from the Security screen, with a PIN or a password of its own (which your fingerprint or face can then stand in for) or with your phone\'s screen lock.

resources.string: Can I use my codes on a computer

Yes, with the CometOTP browser extension, for Chrome, Edge, Brave, Firefox and other browsers. It keeps an encrypted, read-only copy of your services, shows their codes, and can fill them into sign-in pages.

To connect a browser, set a lock in Security first, then go to Security → Connected extensions → Pair a browser and scan the code the extension shows. Pair only if both screens show the same six digits.

Each service has a Browser extension switch in its details, so you choose which ones browsers get. HOTP and mOTP services always stay on your phone. When you change a service, connected browsers get the change.

The copy is encrypted on this phone with a key that only your phone and that browser have, and it goes through a relay that cannot read it. Removing a browser in Connected extensions deletes its copy the next time it checks. A browser that is lost or stolen keeps what it had, so turn two-factor authentication off and on again for those services.

CometOTP is a simple and free two-factor authenticator. It generates time-based one-time passwords (TOTP), counter-based passwords (HOTP), Steam codes and mOTP codes for the services you protect with two-factor authentication.\n\nEverything is stored encrypted on your device and never leaves it unless you create a backup yourself, or connect a browser, which gets an encrypted copy of the services you share with it.
For any other service, look for two-factor authentication or 2-step verification in its security settings.
